etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin ēlīminātus, past participle of ēlīmināre (“to turn out of doors, banish”), from ē (“out”) + līmen (“a threshold”), akin to līmes (“a boundary”); see English limit and limen.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To completely remove, get rid of, put an end to.

quote.citation: 2020 August 4, Jason Schreier, “Blizzard Employees Share Salaries With Each Other to Protest Wage Disparities”, in Time‎[2]:
quote.text: Last year, the company eliminated hundreds of jobs and asked some of the remaining staff to take on the responsibilities of those who were let go.

definitions.definition: (transitive, military) To render (a facility) unusable, to destroy it; to disable (a soldier), make them unable to fight (typically but not necessarily by killing)
(transitive, slang) To kill (a person or animal).

quote.citation: 2015, Ilona Rodan, Sarah Heath, editors, Feline Behavioral Health and Welfare, Elsevier Health Sciences, →ISBN, page 7:
quote.text: In one study, 65.8% of the cat owners relinquishing a cat thought that their cat eliminated outside the litter box or destroyed furniture to spite them.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To exclude (from investigation or from further competition).
(accounting) To record amounts in a consolidation statement to remove the effects of inter-company transactions.[1]
